checks.label: When it happened
checks.nudge: Add when it happened: the date and roughly what time.

ask.instructions: Does the narrative say when the incident happened?

criteria.true: Gives a date, a day or a time of day.

checks.label: Where exactly
checks.nudge: Say exactly where: the site, building, area or aisle, not just the company.

ask.instructions: Does the narrative say specifically where it happened?

criteria.true: Names a site, building, room, area, aisle, address or intersection.
criteria.false: No place, or only a vague one like 'at work'.

checks.label: Who was involved
checks.nudge: Name who was involved, or at least their role (the injured worker, the driver).

ask.instructions: Does the narrative identify who was involved, by name or by role?

criteria.true: Names people or gives their roles, like 'forklift operator Mike Alvarez' or 'a customer'.

checks.label: What they were doing
checks.nudge: Describe the task or activity right before it happened.

ask.instructions: Does it describe what the person was doing right before the incident?

criteria.true: Describes the task or activity underway, like restocking pallets or walking to the exit.
criteria.false: Doesn't say what they were doing.

checks.label: How it happened
checks.nudge: Walk through the sequence: what happened first, what went wrong, how it ended.

ask.instructions: Does it explain how the incident happened, step by step?

criteria.true: Explains the sequence of events and the mechanism, like slipped on fluid and landed on a wrist.
criteria.false: Only states the result, like 'he got hurt'.

checks.label: What contributed
checks.nudge: Mention any condition that contributed: a spill, missing guard, poor lighting, rushing.

ask.instructions: Does it mention a condition or factor that contributed to the incident?

criteria.true: Names a hazard or contributing factor, like a leak, ice, a broken step, glare or a missing guard.

ask.instructions: Does the narrative say that someone was injured?

criteria.true: Someone was hurt, injured or complained of pain.
criteria.false: No injury, or it says no one was hurt.

checks.label: Which body part
checks.nudge: Say which body part was hurt, and which side (left wrist, lower back).

ask.instructions: Does it say which body part was injured?

criteria.true: Names the body part, like wrist, knee, lower back or head.
criteria.false: Doesn't say what part of the body.

checks.label: Care given
checks.nudge: Say what care was given: first aid, clinic, ER, or that none was needed.

ask.instructions: Does it say what medical care or first aid was given?

criteria.true: Mentions first aid, a clinic, ER, ambulance, or that care was declined.

checks.label: Witnesses
checks.nudge: Name any witnesses, or say there were none.

ask.instructions: Does it name witnesses or say there were none?

criteria.true: Names someone who saw it, or says there were no witnesses.

checks.label: What was done after
checks.nudge: Describe what was done right after: area secured, supervisor told, equipment tagged out.

ask.instructions: Does it describe what was done right after the incident?

criteria.true: Describes follow-up actions, like cleaning up, blocking an area, notifying a supervisor or calling police.

checks.label: Blame or opinion
checks.nudge: Stick to what happened. Leave out blame and guesses about attitude (careless, not paying attention).

ask.instructions: Does the narrative assign blame or give opinions instead of facts?

criteria.true: Blames someone or judges them, like 'careless', 'not watching', 'his own fault', 'lazy'.

ask.instructions: How factual and specific is this narrative overall?
criteria: Vague: a sentence or two with few facts.
Some useful facts, with clear gaps.
Specific and factual: an adjuster could act on it.

steps: Mike got hurt in the warehouse.

steps.remove: Mike got hurt in the warehouse.

steps: On Tuesday around 2:30 pm, Mike Alvarez, a forklift operator, was restocking pallets in aisle 7 of Warehouse B.
He stepped off the forklift onto hydraulic fluid that had leaked from the lift, slipped, and landed on his left wrist.
The leak had been reported the day before, but the area was never blocked off.
Shift lead Dana Reyes saw it happen.
He got an ice pack on site and was driven to the Concentra clinic, where they X-rayed his wrist.
We blocked off the aisle, cleaned up the fluid and tagged the forklift out of service.
scenarios.title: Warehouse slip (workers' comp)

steps: A lady fell near the front of the store. She probably wasn't watching where she was going.

steps.remove: She probably wasn't watching where she was going.

steps: It was about 10:15 am on March 3 at our Main St. location, by the entrance mats.
The customer, Joan Pierce, was walking in from the parking lot when her foot caught the curled edge of a rain mat and she fell forward onto her knees.
She said her right knee hurt; a cashier brought her a chair and ice, and she declined an ambulance.
Cashier Luis Ortega saw the fall.
The manager replaced the mat and took photos of the area.
scenarios.title: Customer fall (liability)

steps: On June 9 at about 7:40 am, our delivery driver Sam Ortiz was stopped at the red light at Main and 5th in box truck 214.
A sedan behind him didn't stop in time and hit the rear bumper.
The road was wet from rain. No one was hurt.
A pedestrian, Ana Lim, saw it and gave her number.
Sam called police, swapped insurance with the other driver and photographed both vehicles.
scenarios.title: Fleet fender-bender (auto)
